english: Defeat all bosses on any difficulty.
irish: Defeat gach bosses ar aon deacracht.

english: Defeat all bosses on hard difficulty.
irish: Defeat gach bosses ar deacracht crua.
Amharc ar ár liosta iomlán de shuíomhanna

english: Defeat all bosses on normal difficulty or higher.
irish: Defeat gach bosses ar deacracht gnáth nó níos airde.

english: Defeat all bosses using only your fists.
irish: Defeat gach bosses ag baint úsáide as ach do fists.

english: Eat every kind of edible item.
Embody the spirits of the Toughest Viking, Master Hunter, Survivor and Pathfinder.
irish: Embody an bhiotáille an Lochlannach Thiar, Máistir Hunter, Marthanóir agus Pathfinder.
Die i ngach slí is féidir.

english: You stood a bit too close.

irish: Ní féidir a bheith ina Timpiste

english: Get killed by every kind of tree.
irish: Faigh maraíodh ag gach cineál crann.

english: Travel far in all four directions.
irish: Taisteal i bhfad i ngach ceithre treoracha.

english: Travel far in all four directions, without using a map.
irish: Taisteal i bhfad i ngach ceithre treoracha, gan léarscáil a úsáid.

english: Meet your end, then prepare to do it all again...
irish: Freastal ar do deireadh, ansin a ullmhú chun é a dhéanamh arís...
Maireachtáil ar feadh 30 lá as a chéile.

english: No Adventuring On an Empty Stomach
Sail far enough to circle the world twice.
irish: Sail i bhfad go leor chun ciorcal an domhan faoi dhó.

english: Sail far enough to circle the world, while manning the helm.
irish: Sail i bhfad go leor chun ciorcal ar fud an domhain, agus manning an Helm.

english: Kill every kind of creature on hard difficulty.
irish: Kill gach cineál créatúr ar deacracht crua.

english: Embody the spirits of the Viking, Hunter, Artisan, Master Chef, Carpenter and the Explorer.
irish: Embody an bhiotáille an Lochlannach, Hunter, Artisan, Máistir Chef, Carpenter agus an Explorer.

english: Kill a boss together with a friend.
irish: Kill Boss mar aon le cara.

english: Sail over the edge of the world.
Kill a boss all by yourself.
irish: Kill Boss go léir ag tú féin.

english: This item was summoned through cheating means.
irish: Cuireadh thoghairm an mhír seo trí mheán cheating.

english: That command is a cheat, please enter 'confirmcheats' in the console to use cheats. <color=red>Using cheats will permanently disable the ability to unlock achievements for this character and this world.</color>
irish: Is é sin ordú cheat, le do thoil dul isteach 'confirmcheats' sa console a úsáid cheats. dath = dearg Beidh ag baint úsáide cheats a dhíchumasú go buan ar an gcumas chun éachtaí a dhíghlasáil don charachtar agus an domhan seo r / dath .

english: No more cheated items in inventory. Achievement progress is re-enabled.
irish: Uimh míreanna níos cheated i fardal. Tá dul chun cinn a bhaint amach ath-inúsáidte.

english: Achievement progress is enabled for this character even though dev commands have been used.
irish: Tá dul chun cinn a bhaint amach ar chumas an carachtar cé go bhfuil orduithe dev úsáid.

english: Achievement progress is permanently disabled for this character due to dev command usage.
irish: Tá dul chun cinn a bhaint amach faoi mhíchumas go buan don charachtar mar gheall ar úsáid ordú dev.

english: Achievement progress is permanently disabled for this world due to using dev command world modifiers.
irish: Tá dul chun cinn a bhaint amach faoi mhíchumas go buan don domhan seo mar gheall ar úsáid a bhaint as modifiers domhan ordú dev.

english: Picked up cheated item. Achievement progress is temporarily disabled.
irish: Picked suas mír cheated. Tá dul chun cinn a bhaint amach faoi mhíchumas go sealadach.

english: Achievement progress is temporarily disabled for this character due to possession of cheated items.
irish: Tá dul chun cinn a bhaint amach faoi mhíchumas go sealadach don charachtar mar gheall ar sheilbh míreanna cheated.
An bhfuil a fhios agat na buntáistí a bhaineann...

english: This world contains User Generated Content (UGC) by a player you have blocked. In order to play on this world, you must unblock them. Do you wish to unblock the following user:
irish: Tá an domhan Ábhar Úsáideoir Ginithe (UGC) ag imreoir a bhfuil tú bac. D'fhonn a imirt ar an saol seo, ní mór duit iad a dhíblocáil. An mian leat an t-úsáideoir seo a leanas a dhíbhlocáil:

english: If you believe your ban was issued in error, you may contact our support for review. However, final decisions will be made in accordance with our policies and platform requirements.
irish: Má chreideann tú gur eisíodh do toirmeasc i earráid, féadfaidh tú teagmháil a dhéanamh lenár dtacaíocht le haghaidh athbhreithnithe. Mar sin féin, déanfar cinntí críochnaitheacha de réir ár mbeartas agus ár riachtanais ardán.

english: When playing via crossplay platforms, you’re expected to follow all rules and community guidelines set by us. Please behave at your best.
irish: Agus tú ag imirt trí ardáin tras-imirt, táthar ag súil go leanfaidh tú na rialacha agus na treoirlínte pobail atá leagtha síos againn. Déan iompar ar do chuid is fearr.

english:
We reserve the right to take action against players violating these rules, including:
• Temporary or permanent bans from playing online.
• Restrictions on crossplay features.
irish:
Cúlchiste againn an ceart chun gníomh a ghlacadh i gcoinne imreoirí violating na rialacha, lena n-áirítear:
• Cosc sealadach nó buan ó imirt ar líne.
• Srianta ar ghnéithe tras-imirt.
Imreoir Iompar & Bans - Seinn go freagrach

english: You must also follow the PlayStation™Network’s Community Code of Conduct, which applies in addition to our rules.
irish: Ní mór duit a leanúint freisin Cód Iompair Pobail PlaystationTMNetwork, a bhfuil feidhm aige chomh maith lenár rialacha.

english: You must also follow Xbox's Community Standards, which applies in addition to our rules.
irish: Ní mór duit Caighdeáin Phobail Xbox a leanúint, a bhfuil feidhm acu chomh maith lenár rialacha.

english:
The following actions may result in temporary or permanent bans from playing online:
• Harassment, hate speech, threats, or discrimination.
• Sharing inappropriate or offensive content via chat, in-game building or other means.
irish:
D'fhéadfadh go mbeadh toirmeasc sealadach nó buan ar na gníomhaíochtaí seo a leanas ar líne a imirt:
• Harassment, fuathchaint, bagairtí, nó idirdhealú.
â € ¢ Roinnt ábhar míchuí nó ionsaitheach trí comhrá, i-cluiche foirgneamh nó ar mhodh eile.

english:
If you encounter unacceptable behavior:
• In-game: Use the built-in "Report Player" function (Options->Player List->Report)
• Outside the game: Please use this online form: https://valheim.com/report-a-player
irish:
Má bhíonn tú iompar do-ghlactha:
â € ¢ I-cluiche: Bain úsáid as an-tógtha i "Report Player" fheidhm (Roghanna-bhraise Liosta- ^Report)
• Lasmuigh den chluiche: Bain úsáid as an bhfoirm ar líne seo: https://valheim.com/report-a-player

english: Thank you, warrior. We who lived on in this shape were denied the peace of death for too long. We go now...
irish: Go raibh maith agat, laoch. Shéanadh muid a bhí ina gcónaí ar an cruth seo an tsíocháin an bháis ar feadh ró-fhada. Táimid ag dul anois...

english: So you were my death? You look so small and soft… Tell Oden he may have broken this form but the wilderness will never submit to his rules...
irish: Mar sin, bhí tú mo bháis? Breathnaíonn tú chomh beag agus bog... Déan teagmháil linn D'fhéadfadh sé a bheith briste an fhoirm seo ach ní bheidh an wilderness faoi bhráid a rialacha...

english: Little thing of blood and bone, I should have snapped you like a twig! Now I wither and die, let the great tree have me...
irish: Rud beag fola agus cnámh, ba chóir dom a bheith snapped tú cosúil le craobh! Anois wither mé agus bás, lig an crann mór dom...

english: I followed a false destiny, and it gave me nothing but ruin. Forgive me, my love...
irish: Lean mé destiny bréagach, agus thug sé dom rud ar bith ach ruin. Tabhair dom, mo ghrá...

english: I'm a perch, not a bass!
Once I was free to jump upstream. But no longer.
irish: Nuair a bhí mé saor in aisce chun léim upstream. Ach a thuilleadh.

english: Please lay me to rest by the fire...
irish: Le do thoil a leagan dom a gcuid eile ag an tine...

english: Have you seen my friend around? Her name is Anika.
irish: An bhfaca tú mo chara timpeall? Tá a ainm Anika.

english: You're supposed to put heads on a pike, not put a pike on a wall...
irish: Tá tú ceaptha chun cinnirí a chur ar pike, ní cuir pike ar bhalla...

english: I've got this tune stuck in my head...
irish: Tá mé fuair an tune bhfostú i mo cheann...

english: It's so cold... And dark... But I like it that way.
irish: Tá sé chomh fuar... Agus dorcha... Ach is maith liom é ar an mbealach sin.

english: Stop it with the baiting already!
irish: Stop é leis an bhaoite cheana féin!

english: What's that nasty smell? Surely it couldn't be me!
irish: Cad é go boladh olc? Surely ní fhéadfadh sé a bheith dom!

english: I'm dead but not gone. Won't you free me from this cursed purgatory?
irish: Tá mé marbh ach ní imithe. Ní bheidh tú saor in aisce dom as an purgatory cursed?

english: Do you ever wonder what lurks in the deepest parts of the ocean? Don't. It's better not to know.
irish: An bhfuil tú Wonder riamh cad lurks sna codanna is doimhne de na farraige? Ná. Tá sé níos fearr gan a fhios.

english: Do you see the light? It beckons you...
irish: An bhfeiceann tú an solas? Tá sé beckons tú...
Ná bíodh imní ort. Bí sásta.

english: Take me to the river... Drop me in the water...
irish: Tóg dom go dtí an abhainn... Buail mé san uisce...

english: You think you beat us? Think again... We are still, and forever will be the hive - and the hive is unbeatable.
irish: Sílim go bhfuil tú buille dúinn? Smaoinigh arís... Táimid fós, agus go deo beidh an hive - agus tá an hive unbeatable.

english: Sheathe your pride, creature of Oden! My long reign is at an end but those who come after me are greater still...
irish: Sheathe do bród, creature Oden! Is é mo reign fada ag deireadh ach iad siúd a thagann tar éis dom níos mó fós...

english: Tell Oden that my kin will bring forth another... A monarch never dies.
irish: Déan teagmháil linn Óden go mbeidh mo gaol a thabhairt amach eile... Riamh monarc bás.

english: Do you come to gloat, little thing? Do you know how many times I have been killed, broken, banished, burned and buried? You are not the first and you will not be the last.
irish: An bhfuil tú ag teacht chun gloat, rud beag? An bhfuil a fhios agat cé mhéad uair a maraíodh mé, briste, banished, dóite agus curtha? Níl tú an chéad agus ní bheidh tú an ceann deireanach.

english: You awaken within a dream of dark skies and boiling clouds. Night on the mountaintop, a rough cloak pulled tight around you. Thunder tears the sky and a rain of hot embers pours through the rift, destroying your dream body in an instant…
irish: Dúisigh tú laistigh de bhrionglóid sciálaí dorcha agus scamaill fiuchphointe. Oíche ar an sliabhraonta, clóca garbh tharraing daingean timpeall ort. Thunder deoras an spéir agus báisteach de embers te pours tríd an rift, scriosadh do chorp aisling i toirt...

english: In your sleep, you crouch in the middle of a vast and gloomy cavern while a huge beast prowls in circles around you, dragging the darkness behind it. Emerald flames flicker at its edges and the growl of its throat lingers long into the waking day…
irish: I do chodladh, crouch tú i lár an uaimh ollmhór agus gloomy agus prowls Beast ollmhór i ciorcail timpeall ort, dragging an dorchadas taobh thiar dó. lasracha Emerald flicker ag a imill agus an growl a lingers scornach fada isteach sa lá waking...

english: You dream of eating roast hog at a feast. It is a simple and delicious meal. If only all dreams could be like this.
irish: Aisling tú ag ithe muc rósta ag féasta. Is béile simplí agus delicious. Má d'fhéadfadh ach gach aisling a bheith mar seo.

english: Nine maidens in robes of white dance barefoot at midnight. Nine wolves hunt a white hart in the greenwood. Nine bells ring out on the mountainside and you awake.
irish: Naoi maidens i róbaí rince bán cosnochta ag meán oíche. Naoi wolves fiach hart bán sa greenwood. Naoi bells fáinne amach ar an sliabh agus awake tú.

english: You dream of a hundred ghosts crowding thickly around your bedside, seeking warmth and life until something thumps deep below the ground and they jump like crumbs on a drumskin and are gone.
irish: Aisling tú de chéad thaibhsí crowding thickly thart ar do bedside, ag lorg teas agus an saol go dtí rud éigin thumps domhain faoi bhun na talún agus léim siad cosúil le blúiríní ar drumaskin agus go bhfuil siad imithe.

english: In your dream, you stand naked in the middle of a pool of water so clear it cannot be seen, only felt as a swaying girdle around your hips. Three figures stand at the water's edge, watching you in silence. When the lead figure touches the water's surface with her toe, the ripple dissolves the dream and you wake.
irish: I do bhrionglóid, seasann tú naked i lár an linn snámha uisce chomh soiléir ní féidir é a fheiceáil, ach bhraith mar girdle swaying timpeall do cromáin. Seasann trí fhigiúr ar imeall an uisce, ag faire ort i tost. Nuair a bhíonn an figiúr luaidhe ag baint le dromchla an uisce lena ladhar, díscaoileann an ripple an aisling agus dúisigh tú.

english: You slide down the tunnel of a fretful dream into an absence so complete that no words will cling to it…
irish: Sleamhnán tú síos an tollán aisling aisteach i neamhláithreacht chomh iomlán go mbeidh aon focail cling dó...

english: You dream of a hall in winter, glittering with light and laughter in the midst of a snowy night. As you approach, the lights twist into tall flames and the laughter into screams. You run towards the hall but it sinks hissing into the snow as you approach.
irish: Aisling tú halla sa gheimhreadh, glittering le solas agus gáire i measc oíche snowy. Mar cur chuige tú, na soilse casadh i lasracha ard agus an gáire isteach screams. Rith tú i dtreo an halla ach sinks sé hissing isteach sa sneachta mar a chuireann tú.

english: You run down an endless hill, your heart thumping for joy within your chest. Two dark shapes fly alongside you and the beat of their wings lingers into your waking hours.
irish: Rith tú síos cnoc endless, do thumping croí le haghaidh áthas laistigh de do cófra. Dhá cruthanna dorcha eitilt taobh leat agus an buille a sciatháin lingers isteach i do uair an chloig waking.

english: You see a child's face, laughing and crying at the same time. The eyes are clear and blue behind their tears, the mouth is a tumble of tiny teeth. In the dream, he tells you something, but the words are gone when you wake.
irish: Feiceann tú aghaidh an linbh, ag gáire agus ag caoineadh ag an am céanna. Tá na súile soiléir agus gorm taobh thiar a gcuid deora, is é an béal tumble fiacla beag bídeach. Sa aisling, insíonn sé duit rud éigin, ach tá na focail imithe nuair a osclaíonn tú.

english: In your dream there is a door without pin or bolt. You feel it would open with a push but your body is frozen in a swirl of cold wind. Behind the door are the voices of the ones you love but cannot name. You strain forward into empty wakefulness.
irish: I do bhrionglóid tá doras gan bioráin nó bolt. Braitheann tú go mbeadh sé ar oscailt le brú ach tá do chorp reoite i swirl gaoithe fuar. Taobh thiar den doras iad na guthanna de na cinn grá agat ach ní féidir ainm. Braitheann tú ar aghaidh i múscail folamh.

english: The ghosts of all those who have died at your hand come to you in your sleep and linger at the edges of your dreams. They want nothing, need nothing, say nothing.
irish: Tagann taibhsí na ndaoine go léir a fuair bás ar do lámh leat i do chodladh agus linger ag imill do aisling. Ba mhaith leo rud ar bith, ní gá aon rud, a rá rud ar bith.

english: You sink through layers of sleep to a vast chamber where a dark shape hunches beneath a snarl of heavy chains. As it shifts to face you, the blue orbs of its eyes pierce the dream and you wake, drenched in sweat.
irish: Tá tú doirteal trí sraitheanna codlata go dtí seomra ollmhór ina hunches cruth dorcha faoi bhun snarl de slabhraí trom. Mar a aistríonn sé chun aghaidh a thabhairt ort, an orbs gorm a shúile Pierce an aisling agus dúisigh tú, drenched i allais.

english: You remember nothing of this night's dream but its rainbow mood lifts you into the day with a smile on your lips.
irish: Cuimhnigh tú rud ar bith ar an oíche aisling ach ardaitheoirí a giúmar tuar ceatha tú isteach sa lá le aoibh gháire ar do liopaí.

english: Odin visits you in your dream and offers you a horn filled to the brim with a frothing draught. You drink deep and greet the new day feeling refreshed and alive.
irish: Odin cuairt tú i do bhrionglóid agus cuireann tú adharc líonadh go dtí an brim le dréacht frothing. Deoch tú domhain agus beannú an lá nua mothú athnuachan agus beo.

english:
You dream of running through a meadow, the sky alight with pale fire. There is a thunder of hoofbeats behind you but when you turn, nothing is there.

You awaken with your heart pounding in your chest.
irish:
Aisling tú ag rith trí móinéir, an spéir solas le tine pale. Tá toirneach de hoofbeats taobh thiar duit ach nuair a chasann tú, tá rud ar bith ann.

Dúisigh tú le do chroí pounding i do cófra.

english: In your dream, the forest rises before you, dragging the trees upward like a cloak, its dark mass hiding the stars. At the mountain's peak, vast antlers frame the moon...
irish: I do bhrionglóid, ardaíonn an foraoise roimh tú, dragging na crainn suas cosúil le clóca, a mais dorcha i bhfolach na réaltaí. Ag an sliabh buaic, antlers ollmhór fráma an ghealach...

english:
In your dream, you walk through a hall of smiling warriors and gracious maidens. You join with their mirth until you realise that you are naked and the small bronze shield you are carrying is not enough to cover your shame.

You greet the morning with gratitude.
irish:
I do bhrionglóid, tú ag siúl trí halla de laochra miongháire agus maidens gracious. Tá tú páirteach lena mirth go dtí go realize tú go bhfuil tú naked agus nach bhfuil an sciath cré-umha beag atá tú ag iompar go leor a chlúdach do náire.

beannú tú ar maidin le buíochas.

english:
Dark-eyed Loki approaches you in your dream and gifts you a ring for each hand. He tells you that as long as they stay on your fingers, you will never hear an insulting word again.

You wake with your fingers in your ears.
irish:
Dark-eyed Loki cur chuige tú i do bhrionglóid agus bronntanais tú fáinne do gach lámh. Insíonn sé duit chomh fada agus a fhanann siad ar do mhéara, ní bheidh tú ag éisteacht focal insulting arís.

Dúisigh tú le do mhéara i do chluasa.

english:
You climb a winding staircase, curled tightly within a tall tower, until you arrive at the top and look out over an endless forest.

The wind blows green waves across the tree-tops and beneath the surface, dark shapes stir...
irish:
Dreapann tú staighre foirceannadh, chuir tú go docht laistigh de túr ard, go dtí go dtagann tú ar an mbarr agus féach amach thar foraoise endless.

Na blows gaoithe tonnta glas ar fud na crainn-barr agus faoi bhun an dromchla, cruthanna dorcha stir...

english:
You dream that you are flying over mountaintops, all of Valheim spread out below you.

As you wheel and dive in the cold air, a great shape soars up past you to block the sun. In the darkness, it speaks. "Seek me."
irish:
Aisling tú go bhfuil tú ag eitilt thar sliabhraonta, gach ceann de Valheim scaipeadh amach thíos tú.

Mar tú roth agus Léim san aer fuar, soars cruth mór suas am atá caite tú chun bloc an ghrian. Sa dorchadas, labhraíonn sé. "Seek dom."

english: You dream of a river running uphill, of green shoots turning downward into the earth…
irish: Aisling tú abhainn ag rith suas an cnoc, de shoots glas ag casadh síos isteach sa domhan...

english:
Once again, you run at the head of your warriors, the weight of your father's axe in your hand.

You wake with the war-cry on your lips…
irish:
Arís eile, ritheann tú ag an ceann de do laochra, an meáchan axe do athar i do lámh.

Dúisigh tú leis an gcogadh-crip ar do liopaí...

english:
In your dream, you sit beside a fire in a great hall, surrounded by the chatter of familiar voices.

Their faces blur like smoke and their names slip your mind, but the warmth of their memory lingers…
irish:
I do bhrionglóid, suí tú in aice le tine i halla mór, timpeallaithe ag an comhrá guthanna ar an eolas.

A n-aghaidh blur cosúil deataigh agus a n-ainmneacha duillín d'intinn, ach an teas a lingers cuimhne...

english:
You stand at the prow of a leaping ship, the salt spray before you and the joyful shriek of gulls above.

Folded within a dream, you remember what it was like to be alive in the land of your birth.
irish:
Seasann tú ag an prow ar long leaping, an spraeála salann roimh tú féin agus an shriek joyful de lintéir thuas.

Fillte laistigh de bhrionglóid, cuimhin leat cad a bhí sé cosúil le bheith beo sa talamh ar do bhreith.

english: You dream of a great tree reaching out through the night. One half of its branches crackle with flames, the others are green with leaves.
irish: Aisling tú crann mór a bhaint amach tríd an oíche. Tá leath amháin dá mbrainsí scáinte le lasracha, tá na daoine eile glas le duilleoga.

english:
Amidst the crash of arms, on the dark and glimmering plain of sleep, a face swells snarling before you. Your shield arm hangs limp, your spear is broken. You welcome the cold blade when it comes.

From a dream of death, you awaken to death itself.
irish:
I measc an tuairteála na n-arm, ar an plain dorcha agus glimmering codlata, swells aghaidh snarling roimh tú. Tá do lámh sciath hangs limp, tá do spear briste. Tá tú fáilte roimh an lann fuar nuair a thagann sé.

Ó aisling an bháis, dúisigh tú chun báis féin.

english:
You dream you are lying on your back in a meadow, gazing upward at the clouds. Your name is nothing, your mind is free of thought. But there is a warm hand in yours.

In the dream, you are laughing. But when you awaken, you find your face damp with tears.
irish:
Aisling tú go bhfuil tú suite ar do chúl i móinéir, gazing suas ag na scamaill. Tá d'ainm aon rud, tá d'intinn saor smaoinimh. Ach tá lámh te i mise.

Sa aisling, tá tú ag gáire. Ach nuair a dúisigh tú, gheobhaidh tú do taise aghaidh le deora.

english: On a boat carved from dark wood, beneath ragged sails, you lie with your arms folded across your chest. Blurred faces, like thumbprints on the darkness, croon familiar songs as they push you out to float on a sea as black and flat as glass.
irish: Ar bhád snoite ó adhmad dorcha, faoi bhun seolta ragged, luíonn tú le do arm fillte ar fud do cófra. Aghaidheanna Blurred, cosúil le thumbprints ar an dorchadas, croon amhráin ar an eolas mar a bhrú siad tú amach chun snámh ar farraige mar dubh agus cothrom mar ghloine.

english: You lie on the battlefield, dreaming eyes turned upward to a sky veiled by smoke. The calls of your warriors grow fainter and your eyes close for a second time. Great talons slide beneath you and you feel yourself rising, lifted from your body like a babe from its crib…
irish: Tá tú bréag ar an catha, súile dreaming iompú suas go dtí spéir veiled ag deataigh. Fásann glaonna do laochra níos laige agus do shúile gar don dara huair. Sleamhnán talons Mór faoi bhun tú féin agus bhraitheann tú féin ag ardú, thóg ó do chorp cosúil le babe as a crib...

english: You fall into the deep well of sleep and dream only of darkness.
irish: Tagann tú isteach an dea-domhain codlata agus aisling ach amháin an dorchadais.

english:
You dream of a bright hall filled with gracious warriors and fair maidens. The air hums with song, the boards groan under the weight of steaming dishes, the mead flows like water.

You awake slowly with the laughter still ringing in your ears…
irish:
Aisling tú ar halla geal líonadh le laochra gracious agus maidens cothrom. An hums aer le hamhrán, na boird groan faoi mheáchan na miasa steaming, sreabhadh an mead cosúil le huisce.

Awake tú go mall leis an gáire fós ringing i do chluasa...

english: You sleep in fits and fretful dreams, the weight of the nightmare heavy on your chest. When morning comes, you greet it with relief.
irish: Codlaíonn tú i n-oireann agus aisling greannmhar, meáchan an trom nightmare ar do cófra. Nuair a thagann ar maidin, beannú tú é le faoiseamh.

english: Sleep is a river and dreams are live fish. You wake in the morning with your net empty.
irish: Tá codladh abhainn agus aisling iasc beo. Dúisigh tú ar maidin le do glan folamh.

english:
You dream you are hunting with your companions, running high over green hills and down through mist-haunted valleys. Ahead of you, your prey stumbles and you leap forward, sinking your teeth into warm flesh.

When you wake, the taste of metal lingers in your mouth.
irish:
Aisling tú go bhfuil tú ag fiach le do companions, ag rith ard thar cnoic glas agus síos trí gleannta mist-haunted. Ahead de tú, do stumbles prey agus léim tú ar aghaidh, sinking do chuid fiacla i flesh te.

Nuair a osclaíonn tú, blas na lingers miotail i do bhéal.

english: You dream you are walking in a snowy wood when you come upon a naked child, sitting against a tree with his eyes closed but his chest moving to breathe. As you kneel beside him, you know he has been sleeping here for many centuries, waiting for you. When you touch his shoulder, you both awaken.
irish: Aisling tú go bhfuil tú ag siúl i adhmad snowy nuair a thagann tú ar leanbh naked, ina suí i gcoinne crann lena shúile dúnta ach a cófra ag gluaiseacht a breathe. Mar kneel tú in aice leis, tá a fhios agat go bhfuil sé ag codladh anseo ar feadh na gcéadta bliain go leor, ag fanacht leat. Nuair a dteagmháil leat a ghualainn, tú araon dúisigh.

english: You dream of a mighty bear, sleeping deep below the earth in the winter of the world. It turns in its sleep, folds upon folds of flesh and fur. It has no head, no limbs. A vast mass of bear flesh, mercifully quiet.
irish: Aisling tú ar iompróidh mighty, codlata domhain faoi bhun an domhain i gheimhreadh an domhain. Casadh sé ina codladh, huaire ar huaire de flesh agus fionnadh. Tá sé aon cheann, aon géaga. A mais mór de flesh iompróidh, mercifully ciúin.

english: You fall asleep planning your next day's labor and in your dreams you complete it, hewing wood, foraging for food and hunting after swift deer. You return home exhausted but happy, only to awaken and find the day is still ahead of you...
irish: Tagann tú ina chodladh pleanáil do lá dár gcionn saothair agus i do aisling a chríochnú tú é, adhmad hewing, foraging le haghaidh bia agus fiaigh tar éis fiaigh tapa. Tú ar ais abhaile ídithe ach sásta, ach amháin a mhúscailt agus teacht ar an lá go fóill ar aghaidh leat...

english:
In a chamber hung with golden drapes, you kneel before the throne of a veiled king. "Sleep is but a mask", he tells you, lifting the veil slowly.

You wake screaming.
irish:
I seomra crochadh le drapes órga, tú kneel roimh an ríchathaoir rí veiled. "Tá an chodladh ach masc", insíonn sé duit, ag ardú an veil go mall.

Dúisigh tú screaming.

english:
Wanderer, look to your feet
That tread upon our tomb

english:
His antlers are branches of iron
They crack the rocks and bring down mountains
His hooves are the sound of thunder
His voice a howling gale

Tá a chuid seanóirí brainsí iarainn

english:
A father noble and proud
He soared through skies of fire
Then madness lowered its shroud
And warped his heart's desire
irish:
A athair uasal agus bródúil

Down from the mountain our mother comes
Her weeping tears will fall like rain
Her voice will call us home again

Beidh a deora ag gol titim cosúil le báisteach
Beidh a guth glaoch orainn abhaile arís

english:
First of the Forest, King-in-the-Wood
Lord over those who dwell at his feet
His roots will grow where cities once stood
Their blood his wine, their flesh his meat

An Chéad na Foraoise, Rí-i-an-Wood
Tiarna os cionn iad siúd a dwell ag a chosa
Beidh a chuid fréamhacha ag fás nuair a bhí cathracha uair amháin
A gcuid fola a fíon, a flesh a fheoil

english:

Ruler beneath

english:
Long ages past, he wore a crown
Beneath a blood-red sky
Now naught is left of all he was
But his spirit cannot die

Aois fada anuas, chaith sé coróin

Anois tá dána fágtha ar fad a bhí sé
Ach ní féidir a spiorad bás

english: One person's scrap is another person's treasure.
irish: Is éard atá i gceist le dramh duine amháin stór duine eile.

english: The bow is pulled taut with unreleased power, like the air before a lightning strike.
irish: Tá an bogha ceirteacha tarraingthe le cumhacht gan scaoileadh, cosúil leis an aer roimh stailc lightning.

english: The same mould, yet inclined to yield a more spectacular result... The frost shall reveal all, in time.
irish: An múnla céanna, ach claonadh chun toradh níos iontach a thabhairt... Nochtfaidh an sioc go léir, in am.

english: If your enemies don't freeze as you take aim, they are sure to do so once they are hit.
irish: Más rud é nach bhfuil do naimhde reoite mar a ghlacann tú mar aidhm, tá siad cinnte a dhéanamh mar sin nuair a bhíonn siad buailte.

english: The same mould, yet inclined to yield a more spectacular result... The frost shall reveal all, in time.
irish: An múnla céanna, ach claonadh chun toradh níos iontach a thabhairt... Nochtfaidh an sioc go léir, in am.

english: An incredible force is bound to this weapon, waiting to be unleashed.
irish: Tá fórsa dochreidte faoi cheangal leis an arm seo, ag fanacht le bheith unleashed.

english: This weapon needs to be hardened with frost.
irish: Ní mór an t-arm seo a chruachadh le sioc.

english: Ready to rend your enemies to pieces.
irish: Réidh chun rend do naimhde le píosaí.

english: Rips your foes apart, simple as that.
irish: Rips do foes óna chéile, simplí mar sin.

english: The bolts will tear through your enemies like a particularly nasty gale.
irish: Beidh na boltaí cuimilt trí do naimhde cosúil le gale go háirithe olc.

english: If the bolt doesn't pin your foe in place, the roots surging up from the ground surely will.
irish: Más rud é nach bhfuil an bolt bioráin do foe i bhfeidhm, beidh na fréamhacha surging suas as an talamh surely.

english: A strange power surges within this gem, unlike anything you've felt before.
irish: Tá cumhacht aisteach ag borradh laistigh den tseoid seo, murab ionann agus aon rud a bhraith tú roimhe seo.

english: Partly covered in caked mud, it smells foetid.
irish: Go páirteach clúdaithe i láibe cácaí, boladh sé foetid.

english: A shard of crystal from deep within the earth.
irish: A shard de criostail ó domhain laistigh den domhan.

english: A farming tool for tilling soil.
irish: Uirlis feirmeoireachta chun ithir a chur chun talaimh.

english: Retrieve the seeds from the soil, to plant another time.
irish: Retrieve na síolta ón ithir, a chur am eile.

english: Elastic and strong. This tendon must have come from a quick and agile animal.
irish: leaisteacha agus láidir. Ní mór an tendon tar éis teacht ó ainmhí tapaidh agus agraile.
Mhéadaigh Damáiste do shláinte ar iarraidh

english: Damage increase based on total health missing
irish: Méadú damáiste bunaithe ar shláinte iomlán ar iarraidh

english: Some call it a weed, but it's pretty nonetheless.
irish: Roinnt glaoch air fiaile, ach tá sé go leor nonetheless.
D'íoc an rith sin go léir.

english: A cleaned hide from a deer.
irish: A ghlanadh i bhfolach ó fia.

english: A bound wisp to guide you through the thickest of mists.
irish: A wisp faoi cheangal chun tú a threorú tríd an thickest de mists.

english: Far heavier than it looks, with a faint humming sound from within.
irish: I bhfad níos troime ná mar a bhreathnaíonn sé, le fuaim humming faint ó laistigh.

english: The last frozen tear of a dragon, pulsating with mysterious energy.
irish: An cuimilt reoite deireanach de Dragon, pulsating le fuinneamh mistéireach.

english: An object used to break a Dverger seal.
irish: Réad a úsáidtear chun séala Dverger a bhriseadh.

english: A fragment of a Dvergr sealbreaker.
Looks like a perfect piece for piercing something...
irish: Breathnaíonn cosúil le píosa foirfe do rud éigin piercing...

english: It can hold a lot of mead!
irish: Is féidir é a shealbhú a lán de mead!

english: A restless essence of a once living thing...
irish: Tá croílár restless de rud beo uair amháin...

english: This is the stuff of life, the poison that consumes itself. The Dvergr refine it to use in their esoteric designs.
irish: Is é seo an stuif den saol, an nimh a itheann féin. Déanann an Dvergr é a scagadh chun é a úsáid ina ndearaí esoteric.

english: The fur is dense, coarse, and surprisingly clean.
irish: Tá an fionnadh dlúth, garbh, agus go hiontach glan.

english: A slimy length of something's insides.
irish: A fad slimy de rud éigin ar insides.

english: The smouldering remains of a patriarch.
irish: Tá an smouldering fós de patriarch.

english: Every flying ember is a burning wish to repent.
irish: Tá gach ember eitilt mian dhó a repent.

english: It's hard to tell whether the steam coming off of this dish is because it's freshly cooked or because of the asksvin meat in it. Either way, the spiced meat together with the vineberries and fiddlehead sprouts is so delicious that it doesn't matter!
irish: Tá sé deacair a rá an bhfuil an gaile ag teacht as an mhias seo toisc go bhfuil sé cócaráilte go húire nó mar gheall ar an fheoil asksvin ann. Ceachtar slí, tá an fheoil spiced mar aon leis na fíniúnacha agus na sprouts fidile chomh blasta nach bhfuil sé ábhar!

english: You won't be able to resist this platter of delights from the Black Forest! Venison sirloin steaks are served together with spiced thistles and carrots, and the whole meal is tied together with delicious jams. Just have one more bite!
irish: Ní bheidh tú in ann seasamh in aghaidh an platter de delights ó na Foraoise Dubh! Déantar stéigeanna sirloin a sheirbheáil in éineacht le thistles agus cairéid spiced, agus tá an béile iomlán ceangailte le subh delicious. Just a bhfuil ceann amháin níos mó bite!

english: Warming and filling, this meal will sustain you even during the coldest of days. Porridge and pancakes pair well with jams and sausages, making it hard not to come back for a second helping!
irish: Téamh agus líonadh, beidh an béile a chothú tú fiú le linn na laethanta is fuaire. Porridge agus pancóga péire maith le subh agus ispíní, rud a chiallaíonn sé deacair gan teacht ar ais le haghaidh an dara cuidiú!

english:
Set the table with whatever food and drink you fancy, and impress your guests with a delicious feast.

<color=yellow>Once a feast has been eaten of, it won't return any resources if dismantled.</color>
irish:
Socraigh an tábla le cibé bia agus deoch tú mhaisiúil, agus luí do aíonna le féasta delicious.

dath = buí Nuair a bheidh féasta ithe de, ní bheidh sé ar ais aon acmhainní má dismantled./dath ×

english: <color=yellow>Once a feast has been eaten of, it won't return any resources if dismantled.</color>
irish: <color=yellow>Nuair a bheidh féasta ite de, ní thabharfaidh sé ar ais aon acmhainní má dhíchóimeáiltear é.</color>

english: A boar that has been roasted to perfection, glazed and served atop a bed of greens, with additional cuts of meat on the side. A feast like this is sure to fill your stomach and brighten your day!
irish: Torc a róstadh chun foirfeachta, a gloiníodh agus a seirbheáladh ar bharr leaba ghlas, le gearrthacha breise feola ar an taobh. Is cinnte go líonfaidh féasta mar seo do bholg agus go ngealfaidh sé do lá!
Seomraí Mushrooms Galore á la Mistlands

english: The time has come for mushroom enthusiasts to rejoice! Try different kinds of mushrooms, mushroom marinated seeker meat and mushroom-filled misthare, and don't miss out on the tasty sap dressing.
irish: Tá an t-am teacht le haghaidh díograiseoirí beacán a rejoice! Bain triail as cineálacha éagsúla beacán, marinated beacán feola iarrthóir agus misthare beacán-líonadh, agus ná caill amach ar an cóiriú sap blasta.

english: Gather around this steaming pot full of deliciousness and warm yourselves up again after a day out in the cold. The usually tough and chewey wolf meat has become tender enough to practically melt in your mouth, and the onions and carrots are made even tastier with exciting spices.
irish: Bailigh thart ar an bpota steaming iomlán de deliciousness agus te díbh féin suas arís tar éis lá amach sa fuar. De ghnáth tá feoil mac tíre diana agus chewey tar éis éirí tairisceana go leor chun leá go praiticiúil i do bhéal, agus déantar na oinniúin agus na cairéid fiú níos blasta le spíosraí spreagúil.

english: Fish, fish, and more fish! And also serpent meat, cut to look like fish! Explore the flavours of the Ocean, along with some grilled greens for those still practicing their sea legs.
irish: Éisc, iasc, agus iasc níos mó! Agus freisin feoil nathair, gearrtha chun breathnú cosúil le iasc! Déan iniúchadh ar bhlastáin an Aigéin, chomh maith le roinnt greens grilled dóibh siúd fós ag cleachtadh a cosa farraige.

english: There's nothing plain about this feast! Enjoy pies and loaves fresh from the oven, both sweet and savoury, and experience the culinary equivalent of a hug.
irish: Níl aon rud plain mar gheall ar an feast! Bain sult as cóipeanna agus loaves úr ón oigheann, idir milis agus blasta, agus taithí a fháil ar an coibhéiseach cócaireachta de barróg.

english: Who knew that leeches were edible? With the correct preparation (lots of cooking and lots of seasoning) you will be able to serve them in this feast for the culinary brave. For those who have a sensitive stomach, there are also tasty skewers of sausages and turnips on the side.
irish: Cé a fhios go raibh leeches inite? Leis an ullmhú ceart (liotáin de chócaireacht agus go leor de seasoning) beidh tú in ann chun freastal orthu sa feast do na cróga cócaireachta. Dóibh siúd a bhfuil boilg íogair, tá skewers blasta de ispíní agus torna ar an taobh.

english: This musty stew is a necessity on every adventurer's menu.
irish: Is é seo an stew musty riachtanas ar gach roghchlár fiontaróir ar.

english: High quality wood for fine carpentry.
irish: adhmad ardchaighdeáin le haghaidh siúinéir fíneáil.

english: Plant it to grow a timberwood tree.
irish: Plandaí sé crann adhmaid a fhás.

english: Plant it to grow a fir tree.
irish: Plandaí sé crann lámhaigh a fhás.

english: A tasty side of smoked fish.
Bounty from both land and sea.
irish: Bás ó thalamh agus farraige araon.

english: Some fish already like it where the waters are warm, and this bait brings the temperature close to boiling.
irish: Is maith le roinnt iasc cheana féin nuair a bhíonn na huiscí te, agus tugann an bhaoite seo an teocht gar do fiuchphointe.

english: This bait doesn't look like much, but it's a treat to fish that live where it's cold and dark.
irish: Ní fhéachann an bhaoite seo go mór, ach tá sé ina chóireáil chun iasc a bhfuil cónaí air nuair atá sé fuar agus dorcha.

english: It's not very nutritious, so the only fish that'll take this bait are the ones that are used to just eating ice.
irish: Níl sé an-chothaitheach, mar sin is iad an t-iasc amháin a thógfaidh an bhaoite seo na cinn a úsáidtear chun oighir a ithe.

english: Common dvergr fishing bait. Fishing rod sold separately.
irish: Baoite iascaireachta coitianta dvergr. Slat iascaireachta a dhíoltar ar leithligh.

english: Dead trolls in the forest often attract a fish or two, speed up the process with this bait!
irish: Is minic a mheallann trolls marbh san fhoraois iasc nó dhó, an próiseas a luas leis an mbaoite seo!

english: A bait to guide the fish to you through shrouded waters.
irish: Baoite chun an t - iasc a threorú chugat trí uiscí scriúta.

english: This bait sinks deep, deep enough to lure the fish swimming along the very bottom of the sea.
irish: Cuireann an bhaoite seo go domhain, go domhain go leor chun an snámh éisc a mhealladh feadh bun na farraige.

english: You're not immune to deathsquito bites, and the fish here aren't immune to this snack!
irish: Níl tú díolmhaithe chun bitesquito deathsquito, agus nach bhfuil an t-iasc anseo imdhíonachta leis an sneaic seo!

english: It might smell foul, but the fish drawn to this bait are used to so much worse.
irish: D'fhéadfadh sé boladh bréan, ach úsáidtear an t-iasc a tharraingt chuig an mbaoite seo chun an oiread sin níos measa.

english: Bread and fish, what more to wish?
irish: Arán agus iasc, cad níos mó ar mian leo?

english: These claws will rend flesh and bone alike.
irish: Beidh na crúba a thabhairt ar ais flesh agus cnámh araon.

english: If claws work for wolves, why not for a viking?
irish: Má tá crúba ag obair le haghaidh wolves, cén fáth nach bhfuil le haghaidh inmharthana?

english: A slight risk of frostbite is inevitable.
The same mould, yet inclined to yield a more spectacular result... The frost shall reveal all, in time.
irish: An múnla céanna, ach claonadh chun toradh níos iontach a thabhairt... Nochtfaidh an sioc go léir, in am.

english: A fury comes over you as you fight with these weapons, your blood roaring like thunder in your ears... It seems appropriate.
irish: Tagann fury thar tú agus tú ag troid leis na hairm seo, do chuid fola roaring cosúil le toirneach i do chluasa... Dealraíonn sé cuí.

english: The same mould, yet inclined to yield a more spectacular result... The frost shall reveal all, in time.
irish: An múnla céanna, ach claonadh chun toradh níos iontach a thabhairt... Nochtfaidh an sioc go léir, in am.

english: Wrap your fists in the hardest of metals, to ensure your foes feel the strength behind your blows.
irish: Wrap do fists sa deacra de mhiotail, chun a chinntiú go mbraitheann do foes an neart taobh thiar do blows.

english: This weapon needs to be hardened with frost.
irish: Ní mór an t-arm seo a chruachadh le sioc.

english: According to legend, this metal was used by the gods themselves to craft powerful weapons.
irish: De réir finscéalaíochta, bhain na déithe féin úsáid as an miotal seo chun airm chumhachtacha a cheardú.

english: A withered metal from ancient times. No one knows what it was once used for.
irish: Miotal feoite ón am ársa. Níl a fhios ag aon duine cad chuige ar úsáideadh é tráth.

english: Warm to the touch with glowing veins of strange metal. Needs to be refined in a blast furnace.
irish: Téamh leis an dteagmháil le veins glowing miotail aisteach. Riachtanais a scagadh i foirnéise soinneáin.

english: Unspun fibers from a flax plant.
Can be shaped into sharp blades.
irish: Is féidir é a mhúnlú i lanna géar.

english: These plants carry a strong but pleasant scent. However, it's possible that not all creatures agree...
irish: Déanann na plandaí seo boladh láidir ach taitneamhach. Mar sin féin, is féidir nach n-aontaíonn gach créatúir...

english: This mysterious organ keeps a perfect temperature.
irish: Coinníonn an t-orgán mistéireach teocht foirfe.

english: The saltwater scent of this plant makes you think of the wide open ocean.
irish: Déanann boladh sáile an ghléasra seo smaoineamh ar an aigéan oscailte leathan.

english: Terribly cold to the touch, filled with frozen energy.
irish: Terribly fuar leis an dteagmháil, líonadh le fuinneamh reoite.

english: This magical item needs to be hardened with frost.
irish: Ní mór an mhír draíochta seo a bheith cruaite le sioc.

english: A sturdy kind of wood, excellent for mighty halls.
irish: Tá cineál sturdy adhmaid, den scoth do hallaí mighty.

english: Magic has infused this ice, turning it into something else entirely.
irish: Tá Magic infused an oighear, ag casadh sé isteach rud éigin eile go hiomlán.

english: The last essence of an end once foretold.
irish: An mór inneachar sár-deireadh uair amháin foretold.

english: Light is reflected sharply off of this gem, or does it come from within the stone itself?
irish: Tá solas le feiceáil go géar as an GEM, nó a thagann sé ó laistigh den chloch féin?

english: This gem pulses with energy, almost as if it were a living thing.
irish: An GEM pulses le fuinneamh, beagnach amhail is dá mba rud beo é.

english: You wonder how many deals have been made to appease this gem. How many palms have bled onto it in exchange for its power?
irish: Wonder tú cé mhéad Déileálann déanta a appease seo GEM. Cé mhéad palms a bheith bled isteach air mar mhalairt ar a chumhacht?

english: Channels the ancient power of Yagluth.
Precious metal, infused with the essence of a living thing.
irish: Miotal lómhara, infused leis an croílár rud beo.

english: A hard and sturdy material with plenty of potential. Needs to be refined in a Blast Furnace.
irish: Ábhar crua agus sturdy le neart poitéinseal. Ní mór a scagadh i bhFoirnéis Soinneáin.

english: For a dramatic entrance, or a swift retreat.
irish: Chun bealach isteach drámatúil, nó cúlú tapa.

english: The milky eyeball of a Greydwarf.

irish: Braitheann sé cosúil le iasc coipthe.

english: With this to your hand, you can raise high halls and mighty fortifications.
irish: Leis seo le do lámh, is féidir leat a ardú hallaí ard agus fortifications mighty.

english: A piece of very hard antlers.
Fear not death, for the hour of your doom is set, and no man can escape it.
irish: Fear nach bás, ar feadh uair an chloig de do doom leagtha, agus is féidir aon fhear éalú é.

english: You can keep as quiet as you like, but one day, someone will find you.
irish: Is féidir leat a choinneáil chomh ciúin mar is mian leat, ach lá amháin, beidh duine éigin a fhaigheann tú.

english: No matter how much suffering you went through, you never want to let go of those memories.
irish: Is cuma cé mhéad atá ag fulaingt a chuaigh tú tríd, ní mian leat chun ligean dul ar na cuimhní cinn.

english: When you come out of the storm, you won’t be the same person who walked in. That’s what the storm is all about.
irish: Nuair a thagann tú amach as an stoirm, ní bheidh tú a bheith ar an duine céanna a shiúil i. Sin cad é an stoirm ar fad faoi.

english: A rock feels no pain, and an island never cries.
irish: A bhraitheann carraig aon phian, agus oileán riamh cries.

english: Better to fight and fall than to live without hope.
irish: Níos fearr chun troid agus titim ná chun cónaí gan dóchas.

english: Runes shall you find, and rightly read, of wondrous weight and mighty magic.
irish: Beidh Runes fhaigheann tú, agus ceart a léamh, de mheáchan wondrous agus draíocht mighty.

english: Man cannot discover new oceans unless he has the courage to lose sight of the shore.
irish: Ní féidir le fear a fháil amach aigéin nua mura bhfuil sé an misneach a chailleadh radharc an chladaigh.

english: He who has a why to live can bear almost any how.
irish: Is féidir leis a bhfuil cén fáth chun cónaí iompróidh beagnach aon conas.

english: The wound is the place where the light enters you.
irish: Is é an fhoirceannadh an áit ina dtiocfaidh an solas duit.

english: We suffer more in imagination than in reality.
irish: Táimid ag fulaingt níos mó i samhlaíocht ná i ndáiríre.

english: Pain is inevitable. Suffering is optional.
irish: Tá Pain dosheachanta. Tá fulaingt roghnach.

english: Whatever it is you’re seeking won’t come in the form you’re expecting.
irish: Cibé rud a bhfuil sé go bhfuil tú ag iarraidh nach mbeidh teacht san fhoirm a bhfuil tú ag súil.

english: The meat of a hare is scant but toothsome.
irish: Tá feoil giorria scanta ach toothsome.

english: There's something unsettling about this clotted, frozen mass.
irish: Níl rud éigin unsettling faoi seo clotted, mais reoite.

english: Let the primal rage of a mighty bear consume you.
irish: Lig an rage primal de bear mighty ithe tú.

english: Inspiring fear in foes and courage in kin when worn.
irish: Spreagadh eagla i foes agus misneach i gcnó nuair a chaitear.

english: This will help to keep your brains inside your skull.
irish: Beidh sé seo cabhrú a choinneáil do brains taobh istigh do cloigeann.

english: A bronze helmet with attached horns for extra awesomeness.
irish: Clogad cré - umha le hadharca ceangailte le haghaidh uamhanachta breise.

english: People might say you look like a giant ant. But they will only say it once.
irish: D'fhéadfadh daoine a rá leat breathnú cosúil le ant ollmhór. Ach beidh siad a rá ach uair amháin.

english: You simply can't help but feel happy when donning this cap!
irish: Ní féidir leat ach cabhrú ach a bhraitheann sásta nuair a bhronnadh ar an caipín!

english: A glorious reward for the truly worthy.
irish: A luach saothair glórmhar don fiú fíor.
An Helm ilchasta agus mín - crafted.

english: A portable perpetual lightsource for the dungeon explorer.
irish: Foinse soilse suthain iniompartha don taiscéalaí dungeon.

english: The eyes of the beast were wise and knowing, so that it could measure the strength of a warrior in one glance.
irish: Ba iad na súile an Beast ciallmhar agus a fhios agam, ionas go bhféadfadh sé a thomhas an neart laoch i Sracfhéachaint amháin.

english: This catchy hat may only be reeled in by the most seasoned adventurers.
irish: Is féidir leis an hata catchy a reeled ach amháin ag na fiontaróirí is mó seasoned.

english: While you're wearing this helmet, your enemies will think twice before trying to bite your head off.
irish: Cé go bhfuil tú ag caitheamh an clogad, beidh do naimhde smaoineamh faoi dhó sula ag iarraidh a bite do cheann amach.

english: This armour needs to be hardened with frost.
irish: Ní mór an t-arm seo a chruachadh le sioc.

english: A simple yet fashionable purple cap.
irish: A caipín corcra simplí fós faiseanta.

english: A warm fur cap, made from the finest leather.
irish: Caipín fionnaidh te, déanta as an leathar is fearr.

english: A warm cap for special occasions.
A simple yet fashionable red cap.
irish: A caipín dearg simplí fós faiseanta.

english: A warm fur cap, made from the finest wool.
irish: Caipín fionnaidh te, déanta as an olann is fearr.

english: A warm cap for special occasions.
Embellished with the wings of victory.
irish: Embellished leis na sciatháin an bua.

english: This armour needs to be hardened with frost.
irish: Ní mór an t-arm seo a chruachadh le sioc.

english: A helm of polished iron, fit for a hero.
irish: A Helm d'iarann snasta, oiriúnach do laoch.

english: See the world like a lox might.
irish: Féach ar an domhan mar a d'fhéadfadh lox.

english: Even the first sorceress valued the mystique of covering one's face. It is rumoured that honouring her this way will make your spells even more powerful.
irish: Fiú an chéad sorceress luacháil an mystique de chlúdach amháin ar aghaidh. Tá sé rumoured go onóir a mbealach seo a dhéanamh do geasa fiú níos cumhachtaí.

english: The spirits of the land come as you beckon. Are they fooled by your disguise?
irish: Tagann biotáille na talún mar beckon tú. An bhfuil siad fooled ag do cheilt?

english: Sorcery shows itself in the eyes, so most mages wear cowls to disguise their occult pursuits.
irish: Léiríonn Sorcery féin sna súile, mar sin an chuid is mó mages a chaitheamh cowls a cheilt a gcuid tóir occult.

english: This armour needs to be hardened with frost.
irish: Ní mór an t-arm seo a chruachadh le sioc.

english: As the first man of Midgard, Ask knew it was important to not draw too much attention to himself.
irish: Mar chéad fhear Midgard, bhí a fhios ag Ask go raibh sé tábhachtach gan an iomarca airde a tharraingt air féin.

english: Something to protect your neck from the elements as well as from the sharp teeth of the enemy.

english: Dance with death as you dodge your enemies' strikes.
irish: Rince le bás mar dodge tú do naimhde' stailceanna.

english: Claw and bone and gold – grant them blood and they shall grant you a boon.
irish: Claw agus cnámh agus ór – iad a dheonú fola agus beidh siad a dheonú duit boon.

english: They say that the soul of a witch can grant strange powers to mortals...
irish: Deir siad gur féidir leis an anam medicine cumhachtaí aisteach a dheonú do mortals...

english: It pulsates with fragments of ancient life.
irish: pulsates sé le blúirí den saol ársa.

english: A beautiful pendant, harbouring the endurance of a bear.
irish: A pendant álainn, harbouring an endurance de béar.

english: If you listen carefully, you can hear the faint echoes of lost souls...
irish: Má tá tú ag éisteacht go cúramach, is féidir leat a chloisteáil na macallaí faint de anamacha caillte...

english: Empty your mind as you become shapeless and one with the water.
irish: Folamh d'intinn mar a bheith tú shapeless agus ceann leis an uisce.

english: It's warm, as if filled with a lifesblood of its own.
irish: Tá sé te, amhail is dá mba líonadh le lifesblood dá chuid féin.

english: Puts a spring in your step!
A razor-sharp ankle chain. Can it truly be comfortable?
irish: A slabhra rúitín rásúr - géar. An féidir é a bheith fíor - chompordach?

english: Assume the sharp and furious mind of a wolf.
irish: Glac leis an aigne géar agus ar buile mac tíre.

english: A shard of frozen sorrow. Touching it makes you feel almost numb.
irish: Siord de bhrón reoite. Teagmháil a dhéanann sé bhraitheann tú beagnach numb.

english: A thick and sturdy hide. This is why trolls are so hard to kill.
irish: A cheilt tiubh agus sturdy. Sin é an fáth go bhfuil trolls chomh deacair a mharú.

english: A tangled mess of roots and bark.
irish: Tá praiseach tangled de fréamhacha agus coirt.

english: It's been dead so long that it started living again.
irish: Tá sé marbh chomh fada agus a thosaigh sé ag maireachtáil arís.

english: Don't let yourself be fooled by the friendly smile, for it could easily bite your arm off.
irish: Ná lig tú féin a bheith fooled ag an aoibh gháire cairdiúil, d'fhéadfadh sé a bite go héasca do lámh as.

english: A mighty beast, but now it shall roam no more.
irish: A Beast mighty, ach anois beidh sé roam nach bhfuil níos mó.

english: The frozen head of a once-living tree.
A forest creature, metamorphosed into living frost.
irish: Créatúr foraoise, meiteamorfach ina shioc beo.
Is é sin stare fós scanrúil...

english: Mistakenly, it believed itself the master of the forest.
irish: Mistakenly, chreid sé féin an máistir na foraoise.

english: These eyes are finally vacant for good.
irish: Tá na súile folamh ar deireadh le haghaidh maith.

english: The most dreaded shadow of the night.
irish: An scáth is dreaded ar an oíche.

english: A smelly lump of sticky matter.
It's like a shard of ice, only...slimy?
irish: Tá sé cosúil le shard oighir, ach... caol?

english: No matter the passage of time, it remains frozen.
irish: Is cuma an sliocht ama, tá sé reoite.

english: Even now, it's burning hot to the touch.
irish: Fiú anois, tá sé ag dó te leis an dteagmháil.

english: Remains of unfortunate adventurers, digested and jellified over time.
irish: Taisí de fiontaróirí trua, digested agus jellified le himeacht ama.

english: It still jiggles, but you're fairly certain that it's dead.
irish: Tá sé fós míreanna mearaí, ach tá tú cinnte go bhfuil sé marbh.

english: This boar head would make for a nice decoration in any house.
irish: Bheadh an ceann boar a dhéanamh le haghaidh maisiú deas in aon teach.

english: Any viking worth their axe should know how to slay a boar.
irish: Ba chóir go mbeadh a fhios ag aon viking fiú a tua conas torc a mharú.

english:
Bones and viscous goo, held together by some unseen force.

Offer it to the Sacrificial Stones.
irish:
Bones agus goo slaodach, ar siúl le chéile ag roinnt fórsa unseen.

Déan é a thairiscint do na Clocha Íobairt.

english: A mess of black soil and old bone, thankfully quiet now.
irish: Praiseach d'ithir dhubh agus de sheanchnámh, buíochas le Dia ciúin anois.

english: A skull made up of dense bone, as dangerous as it is protective.
irish: Cloigeann déanta suas de chnámh dlúth, chomh contúirteach is atá sé cosantach.

english: These jagged teeth had been the death of many a seafarer, before the beast finally met its own end.
irish: Bhí na fiacla jagged an bás go leor maraithe, roimh bhuail an Beast ar deireadh a deireadh féin.

english: The younger of two brothers. Jealous of his brother's magic.
irish: An óige de bheirt deartháireacha. Jealous draíochta a dheartháir.

english: These legs could hold infinite power.
irish: D'fhéadfadh na cosa a shealbhú cumhacht gan teorainn.
Marches an saighdiúir seo níos mó.

english: A warm glow seems to almost emanate from within. Handle with care.
irish: Is cosúil go n - eascraíonn glow te beagnach ón taobh istigh. Láimhseáil go cúramach.

english: If you listen closely, you can still hear the faint hum of magic.
irish: Má tá tú ag éisteacht go dlúth, is féidir leat a chloisteáil fós ar an hum faint de draíochta.

english: Fractures line this skull, as if it has taken many hits over the years.
irish: Fractures líne seo cloigeann, mar má tá sé tógtha amas go leor thar na blianta.

english: Even in death, its gaze is unrelenting.
irish: Fiú amháin i bás, tá a gaze gan staonadh.

english: My, what big teeth it has...
irish: Mo, cad fiacla mór tá sé...

english: He's giving you an icy stare.
irish: Tá sé ag tabhairt tú stare icy.

english: Isolated from his kin for embracing the white frost instead of resisting it.
irish: Isolated as a kin chun glacadh leis an sioc bán in ionad a seasamh in aghaidh é.

english: The fire in its eyes has still not burned out.
irish: Níl an tine ina súile dóite fós amach.

english: You don't like touching this thing even when it's dead.
irish: Ní maith leat touching an rud seo fiú nuair a tá sé marbh.

english: It's strange that we should suffer so much over so small a thing.
irish: Tá sé aisteach gur chóir dúinn ag fulaingt an oiread sin níos mó ná sin beag rud.

english: A fine specimen, but you'll need to kill more than deer to enter Valhalla.
irish: A eiseamal breá, ach beidh ort a mharú níos mó ná fianna chun dul isteach Valhalla.

english: Seemingly identical to the ones found in Midgard.
irish: Seemingly comhionann leis na cinn le fáil i Midgard.

english:
The head of a dragon, majestic even in the rigor of death.

Offer it to the Sacrificial Stones.
irish:
An ceann de Dragon, maorga fiú i rigor an bháis.

Déan é a thairiscint do na Clocha Íobairt.

english: Scored with ancient scars, this head was the last sight of countless warriors.
irish: Scortha le scars ársa, bhí an ceann an radharc deireanach de laochra countless.

english: Bind up the mouth if it starts to whisper in the night...
irish: Ceangail suas an béal má thosaíonn sé a whisper san oíche...

english: What should have been left to rest in peace has been awoken, twisted and corrupted.
irish: Cad ba chóir a bheith fágtha chun sosa a bhí awoken, twisted agus truaillithe.

english: The dead stare of the glowing red eyes sends a shiver through your bones.
irish: Cuireann an stare marbh de na súile dearg glowing shiver trí do chnámha.

english: Perhaps this was once a mighty warrior, worthy of praise. Now it is but a rotten, horrid corpse.
irish: B'fhéidir go raibh sé seo uair amháin ina laoch mighty, fiú moladh. Anois tá sé ach rotten, horrid corpse.

english: It's frankly a little troubling that you would consider hanging these on your wall...
irish: Tá sé frankly troubling beag go mbeadh tú a mheas crochta na ar do bhalla...

english:
This severed head oozes power.

Offer it to the Sacrificial Stones.
irish:
Seo oozes ceann déine cumhachta.

Déan é a thairiscint do na Clocha Íobairt.

english: Once the king of the forest, the size of the antlers is truly impressive.
irish: Nuair a bheidh an rí na foraoise, is é an méid de na antlers fíor go hiontach.

english: Mean little eyes stare back at you.
irish: Mean súile beag stare ar ais ag tú.

english: Was it driven by cruelty or mischief? We may never know.
irish: An raibh sé tiomáinte ag cruálacht nó mischief? Ní féidir linn a fhios.

english:
This severed head oozes power.

Offer it to the Sacrificial Stones.
irish:
Seo oozes ceann déine cumhachta.

Déan é a thairiscint do na Clocha Íobairt.

english: Even in death, it seems to grin with secret knowledge.
irish: Fiú amháin i bás, is cosúil go grin le eolas rúnda.

english:
The green dragon, corrupted beyond redemption.

Offer him to the sacrificial stones.
irish:
An dragan glas, truaillithe thar fhuascailt.

Tairiscint dó go dtí na clocha íobartach.

english: Only tatters remained of his sane mind. Perhaps it was a mercy to kill him.
irish: Ach tatters fhan a aigne sane. B'fhéidir go raibh sé trócaire a mharú dó.

english: Though she is dead, she yearns for the blood to flow.
irish: Cé go bhfuil sí marbh, yearns sí don fhuil a sreabhadh.

english: Once a fierce and noble being, before she was warped into a harbinger of terror.
irish: Nuair a bheith fíochmhar agus uasal, sula raibh sí warped i harbinger terror.

english: A strange, elongated paw, its claws razor sharp.
irish: A aisteach, fadálach lapa, a crúba rásúr géar.

english: Halfway between wolf and man, forever frozen in a snarl of pain.
irish: Leathbhealach idir mac tíre agus fear, go deo reoite i snarl pian.

english: The leathery skin bears the faded tracery of ancient symbols.
irish: Bears an craiceann leathair an rianaithe faded na siombailí ársa.

english: The leathery skin bears the faded tracery of ancient symbols.
irish: Bears an craiceann leathair an rianaithe faded na siombailí ársa.

english: The eyes still glitter and swirl with silvery flecks. Don't look into them for too long...
irish: Na súile fós glitter agus swirl le flecks silvery. Ná breathnú isteach orthu ar feadh ró-fhada...

english: The eyes still glitter and swirl with silvery flecks. Don't look into them for too long...
irish: Na súile fós glitter agus swirl le flecks silvery. Ná breathnú isteach orthu ar feadh ró-fhada...

english: Does it still whisper about unfinished business?
irish: An bhfuil sé fós whisper faoi ghnó neamhchríochnaithe?

english: There is still something haunting about its presence...
irish: Tá fós rud éigin haunting mar gheall ar a láithreacht...
Tá súil againn nach mbeidh sé snámh ar shiúl.

english: A most peculiar creature, shaped by a most peculiar place.
irish: Créatúr is peculiar, múnlaithe ag áit is peculiar.

english: Loose folds of greenish skin gathered in around a pair of dark and hateful eyes.
irish: Fillteán caillte de chraiceann greenish a bailíodh i thart ar péire de na súile dorcha agus hateful.

english: Sometimes, you swear you can still hear its echoing laughter.
irish: Uaireanta, swear tú is féidir leat a chloisteáil fós a gáire macalla.

english: The huge grizzled head is as heavy as a boulder.
irish: Is é an ceann grizzled ollmhór chomh trom mar bhollán.

english: Praised for its strength, it lived only to defend its village.
irish: Mholadh as a neart, bhí cónaí air ach amháin chun a sráidbhaile a chosaint.

english:
The crownless head of a dead king.

Offer it to the Sacrificial Stones.
irish:
An ceann crownless rí marbh.

Déan é a thairiscint do na Clocha Íobairt.

english: Sometimes, the eyes still move and the lips mutter silently...
irish: Uaireanta, na súile bogadh go fóill agus na liopaí mutter go ciúin...

english: It shall cast no more spells against you.
irish: Ní chaithfidh sé geasa níos mó in aghaidh leat.

english: Even killing it couldn't wipe the knowing smile from its crooked lips...
irish: Fiú marú ní fhéadfadh sé wipe an aoibh gháire a fhios agam as a liopaí cam...

english: The mossy, severed head of a Greydwarf.
irish: An ceann caonach, déine de Greydwarf.

english: Woe be upon those who disturb their forests...
irish: Mairg a bheith orthu siúd a cur isteach ar a gcuid foraoisí...

english: It took seven blows to hack this gnarled head from its body.
irish: Thóg sé seacht blows a hack an ceann gnarled as a chorp.

english: Roots and stones, twisted by dark intents.
irish: Roots agus clocha, twisted ag intinn dorcha.

english: It may try to come back so be sure to prune any new shoots...
irish: D'fhéadfadh sé iarracht teacht ar ais mar sin a bheith cinnte go prune aon shoots nua...

english: Primal magic once coursed through it. Perhaps some still lingers...
irish: Draíocht Primal le linn uair amháin tríd. B'fhéidir roinnt lingers fós...

english: Whatever brought this creature to life is now long gone.
irish: Cibé rud a thug an creature don saol anois imithe fada.

english: These are said to bring luck. But not for their original owner.
irish: Tá siad seo a rá a thabhairt luck. Ach ní le haghaidh a n-úinéir bunaidh.

english: A rather odd animal, of both scale and fur.
irish: Ainmhí sách corrach, ar scála agus fionnaidh araon.

english: A young dragon – hopefully its mother will not seek vengeance.
irish: A dragan óg – tá súil againn nach mbeidh a mháthair a lorg vengeance.

english: Once a mighty warrior, now nought but a husk remains.
irish: Nuair a ghaiscíoch mighty, anois nought ach fanann husk.

english: A hardened soldier. What battles has he witnessed?
irish: Saighdiúir cruaite. Cad iad na cathanna a chonaic sé?

english: Before her death, her eyes sparked with magic. Now they're empty and void.
irish: Roimh a bás, Sparked a súile le draíocht. Anois tá siad folamh agus ar neamhní.

english: A powerful witch. What strange mysteries was she privy to?
irish: Cailleach chumhachtach. Cad iad na mistéirí aisteacha a raibh sí ag príobháidiú chucu?

english: Although slimy, the skin is beautifully patterned in red and black.
irish: Cé go slimy, tá an craiceann álainne patterned i dearg agus dubh.

english: A whole life spent in a dark swamp, now come to an untimely end.
irish: A saol ar fad a chaitear i swamp dorcha, teacht anois chun deiridh anabaí.

english: A giant beast's head, thatched with thick fur.
irish: Ceann beithíoch ollmhór, tuí le fionnadh tiubh.

english: A beast capable of both loyalty and destruction.
irish: Beithíoch atá in ann dílseacht agus scrios araon a dhéanamh.

english: Getting slashed by these claws would be very unpleasant.
irish: Bheadh Getting slashed ag na crúba a bheith an-áitneamhach.

english: This eyeless one shall dig no more.
irish: Ní rachaidh an duine seo níos mó.

english: The mighty ruler of the northern forests.
irish: An rialóir mighty na foraoisí thuaidh.

english: A majestic beast, and an iconic piece of decor.
irish: Beithíoch maorga, agus píosa íocónach maisiúchán.

english: The waking nightmare has met its end.
irish: Tá an nightmare waking bhuail a deireadh.

english: Only the most twisted of minds could summon such a creature.
irish: Ach d'fhéadfadh an chuid is mó twisted aigne a thoghairm den sórt sin a creature.

english: The beady eyes and razor sharp teeth belie the ostensibly calm nature of this small lizard.
irish: Na súile beady agus fiacail géar rásúir belie an nádúr socair ostensibly an lizard beag.

english: These creatures thrive in water, until a viking lands on their shores.
irish: Na créatúir thrive in uisce, go dtí tailte inmharthana ar a gcladach.

english: This animal never did any harm, yet it met an untimely end.
irish: Ní raibh an t-ainmhí aon dochar, ach bhuail sé deireadh untimely.

english: Those big, sad eyes stare back at you. What have you done?
irish: Glacfar mór, súile brónach stare ar ais ag tú. Cad a rinne tú?

english: The head of a fallen champion.
irish: An ceann de curadh tar éis titim.

english: The strongest of the brood, raised to be a mighty warrior.
irish: An láidre an ál, ardaíodh a bheith ina laoch mighty.

english: Less delicate than they look. The leather of the wings catches the firelight as if remembering flight.
irish: Níos lú íogair ná mar a fhéachann siad. An leathar na sciatháin gabhálacha an tine mar má cuimhneamh eitilt.

english: Relying on sound rather than sight, this creature was a most dangerous foe in the fog.
irish: Ag brath ar fhuaim seachas radharc, bhí an créatúr foe is contúirtí sa ceo.

english:
She has seen enough.

Offer it to the Sacrificial Stones.
irish:
Tá sí le feiceáil go leor.

Déan é a thairiscint do na Clocha Íobairt.
Tá sí le feiceáil go leor.

english: The scales have dulled but the eyes are still bright.
irish: Tá na scálaí tar éis dul ach tá na súile fós geal.

english: It ruled the seas unchallenged – until now.
irish: Rialaigh sé na farraigí unchallenged – go dtí anois.

english: This crystalline rock formation would make for an impressive floor decoration.
irish: Bheadh an foirmiú carraig criostalach a dhéanamh le haghaidh maisiú urlár go hiontach.

english: Rock and crystal, brought to life by ancient magic.
irish: Rock agus criostail, a thabhairt ar an saol ag draíocht ársa.

english: In the choice of 'ride or die', he picked the latter.
irish: Sa rogha 'bród nó bás', phioc sé an dara ceann.

english: The elder brother. Wished he had his brother's strength.
irish: An deartháir elder. Wished bhí sé neart a dheartháir.

english: The expressionless grin of this skull reminds you of the inevitability of death.
irish: An grin expressionless an cloigeann gcuimhne duit ar an dosheachanta an bháis.

english: Her rage burned so hot it stayed with her after death.
irish: A rage dóite chomh te d'fhan sé léi tar éis bháis.

english: It died and then rose again. Is this the fate that awaits you?
irish: Fuair sé bás agus ansin d'ardaigh arís. An bhfuil sé seo an chinniúint go fanacht leat?
An bhfuil a fhios agat na buntáistí a bhaineann...

english: A rank and rotten skull. You're not sure why you kept it...
irish: A céim agus cloigeann lofa. Níl tú cinnte cén fáth ar choinnigh tú é...

english: To end its lingering existence was most likely a mercy.
irish: Chun deireadh a bheith ann lingering is dócha trócaire.

english: Wreathed in pale flame, it still smoulders like an ember.
irish: Wreathed i lasair pale, smoulders sé fós cosúil le ember.

english: A fiendish creature, born of fire.
irish: Créatúr fiendish, a rugadh de thine.

english: Perhaps one of the most nasty things you have encountered. Fortunately, it's dead!
irish: B'fhéidir ar cheann de na rudaí is olc agat a bhíonn. Fortunately, tá sé marbh!

english: The leathery skin bears the faded tracery of ancient symbols.
irish: Bears an craiceann leathair an rianaithe faded na siombailí ársa.

english: Though this world is its domain, you have proven it can be defeated.
irish: Cé go bhfuil an domhan a bhfearann, tá tú cruthaithe is féidir é a defeated.
Foinse do bhfianaise faoi stiúir glan

english: A rugged tail from a not so good boy.
irish: A eireaball garbh ó bhuachaill nach bhfuil chomh maith.

english: Despite its bestial nature, there was something intelligent about it.
irish: In ainneoin a nádúr bestial, bhí rud éigin cliste mar gheall air.

english: It's like a vulture, but it thrives in volcanic climates.
irish: Tá sé cosúil le vulture, ach thrives sé i climates bholcánach.

english: Its watchful eyes still seem to search for cadavers to feast upon.
irish: Is cosúil go bhfuil a súile watchful fós chun cuardach a dhéanamh ar cadavers chun feast ar.

english: Frozen in death, the hair matted with blood and a silent howl lodged in its throat.
irish: Frozen i bás, an ghruaig matted le fuil agus howl adh dtaiscfear ina scornach.

english: This animal has the potential to be a viking's greatest friend – or their greatest enemy.
irish: Tá an t-ainmhí an poitéinseal a bheith ina viking ar cara is mó - nó a namhaid is mó.

english: The shed skin of a wraith, a flowing robe only visible by moonlight.
irish: An craiceann a chaillfidh de wraith, gúna ag sileadh le feiceáil ach amháin ag moonlight.

english: At last, this restless spirit has been set free.
irish: Ag seo caite, tá an spiorad restless leagtha saor in aisce.

english: Tough dead, it should probably be handled delicately.
irish: Tough marbh, ba chóir é a láimhseáil dócha delicately.

english: It remains dormant, at least for now...
irish: Tá sé fós díomhaoin, ar a laghad le haghaidh anois...

english: A dense vegetable, rich with nutrition.
These can be planted in cultivated soil.
irish: Is féidir iad seo a chur in ithir saothraithe.

english: Your attacker shall stand no chance as this missile finds its target.
irish: Beidh do ionsaitheoir seasamh aon seans mar a fhaigheann an diúracán a sprioc.

english: These thick missiles can punch through the hide of even the toughest foes.
irish: Is féidir leis na diúracáin tiubh punch tríd an cheilt ar fiú na foes toughest.

english: Forged from one of the hardest metals in all of Valheim, this missile is sure to hold off your enemies.
irish: brionnaithe ó cheann de na miotail is deacra i ngach ceann de Valheim, tá an diúracán cinnte a shealbhú amach do naimhde.
An bhfuil a fhios agat na buntáistí a bhaineann...

english: Sturdy wooden missiles that can provide a tough defense against foes.
irish: Sturdy diúracáin adhmaid is féidir a chur ar fáil cosaint diana i gcoinne foes.

english: This mysterious idol is brimming with the potential of the gods. It could grant a powerful boon, or demand a great sacrifice.
irish: Tá an idol mistéireach brimming leis an acmhainneacht na déithe. D'fhéadfadh sé a dheonú boon cumhachtach, nó éileamh íobairt mór.

english: A sweet and tasty treat, to celebrate a feat!
irish: A chóireáil milis agus blasta, chun ceiliúradh a dhéanamh ar feat!

english: These juicy berries are both sour and sweet.
irish: Tá na caora juicy seo géar agus milis.

english: Looks like they could crumble at any moment.
irish: Breathnaíonn mar a d'fhéadfadh siad crumble ag am ar bith.

english: These unassuming seeds can grow into vines that might overtake entire buildings.
irish: Is féidir leis na síolta a glacadh ag fás i fíniúnacha a d'fhéadfadh a overtake foirgnimh ar fad.

english: A chewy and somewhat dry meat. Some seasoning would probably make it taste better, but it'll fill your stomach regardless.
irish: Feoil chewy agus beagán tirim. Bheadh roinnt seasoning dhéanamh dócha go bhfuil sé blas níos fearr, ach beidh sé a líonadh do boilg beag beann.

english: Given that this bird feasts on all kinds of things, you'd better cook its meat before you even think about eating it.
irish: Ós rud é go féastaí éan seo ar gach cineál rudaí, ba mhaith leat cócaireacht níos fearr a fheoil sula gceapann tú fiú faoi é a ithe.

english: Warm to the touch, and full of protein.
irish: Téamh leis an dteagmháil, agus iomlán de próitéin.

english: This ancient bone remembers the location of many forgotten things.
irish: Cuimhníonn an cnámh ársa an suíomh go leor rudaí dearmad.

english: A giant bone, knotted like old wood.
irish: Cnámh ollmhór, snaidhmthe cosúil le sean - adhmad.

english: It is hard and sharp like iron.
irish: Tá sé crua agus géar cosúil le iarainn.

english: A bundle of thick, rough hair. It has a strong smell.
irish: Beart de ghruaig thiubh, gharbh. Tá boladh láidir air.

english: Good, strong wood to build with.
irish: Dea, adhmad láidir a thógáil leis.

english: The gnarled body parts of a strange, offputting creature.
irish: Na codanna comhlacht gnarled de aisteach, aschur creature.

english: The remains of Yagluth, a twisted spirit torn between this world and the next.
irish: An iarsmaí de Yagluth, torn spiorad twisted idir an saol seo agus an chéad cheann eile.

english: Made with sap from the great tree. Even a mouthful imparts a warm glow to your whole body.
irish: Déanta le holc ón gcrann mór. Fiú mouthful Tugann glow te do chorp ar fad.

english: Godflesh, wood from the Great Tree.
irish: Godflesh, adhmad as an Crann Mór.

english: The earthy remains of the giant Ymir.
irish: Tá an t-ollmhór fós ar an Ymir ollmhór.
Téigh go dtí na suíomhanna eile:
Foinse do bhfianaise faoi stiúir glan
Foinse do bhfianaise faoi stiúir glan

english: A very small percentage of individuals may experience epileptic seizures when exposed to certain visual images, including light patterns or flashing lights that may appear in video games or other video content. Exposure to certain patterns or backgrounds on a computer screen, or while playing video games, may induce an epileptic seizure in these individuals. Certain conditions may induce previously undetected epileptic symptoms even in persons who have no history of prior seizures or epilepsy.
irish: D'fhéadfadh céatadán an-bheag de dhaoine aonair taithí taomanna epileptic nuair a nochtar le híomhánna amhairc áirithe, lena n-áirítear patrúin éadroma nó soilse gealánacha a d'fhéadfadh a bheith le feiceáil i cluichí físeáin nó ábhar físe eile. Nochtadh do phatrúin áirithe nó cúlraí ar scáileán ríomhaire, nó ag imirt cluichí físeáin, d'fhéadfadh a spreagadh urghabháil epileptic sna daoine aonair. D'fhéadfadh coinníollacha áirithe a aslú roimhe comharthaí epileptic undetected fiú i ndaoine nach bhfuil aon stair na taomanna roimh ré nó titimeas.

english: If you, or anyone in your family, have an epileptic condition, consult your physician prior to playing Valheim. If you experience any of the following symptoms while playing - dizziness, altered vision, eye or muscle twitches, loss of awareness, disorientation, any involuntary movement, or convulsions - discontinue IMMEDIATELY and consult your physician before resuming use of Valheim.
irish: Má tá tú, nó duine ar bith i do theaghlach, tá riocht epileptic, i gcomhairle do dochtúir roimh imirt Valheim. Má bhíonn tú aon cheann de na comharthaí seo a leanas agus iad ag imirt - meadhrán, athrú fís, súl nó muscle twitches, caillteanas feasachta, disorientation, aon ghluaiseacht neamhdheonach, nó convulsions - scor IMMEDIATELY agus dul i gcomhairle le do dochtúir roimh úsáid a bhaint as Valheim.

english: PHOTOSENSITIVE SEIZURE WARNING: READ BEFORE PLAYING
This game has an autosave feature. Please don't turn off the game or console when you see the autosave icon.
irish: Tá an cluiche gné autosave. Ná cas amach an cluiche nó consól nuair a fheiceann tú an deilbhín autosave.

english: Don't forget to upgrade your crafting stations, weapons and armour.
irish: Ná déan dearmad a uasghrádú do stáisiúin crafting, airm agus armúr.

english: Eating food increases your health and stamina pools. Try to balance your three food slots accordingly.
irish: Eating bia méaduithe do shláinte agus stamina linnte. Bain triail as a chothromú do thrí sliotáin bia dá réir.

english: Upgraded stations enable various crafting options and let you improve your equipment.
irish: Cuireann stáisiúin uasghrádaithe ar chumas roghanna éagsúla ceardaíochta agus lig duit do threalamh a fheabhsú.

english: There are four principal crafting types: woodworking, masonry, smithing, and cooking.
irish: Tá ceithre phríomhchineál crafting: adhmadóireachta, masonry, smithing, agus cócaireachta.

english: Enemies won't spawn near player built structures, such as crafting tables and camp fires.
irish: Ní bheidh Enemies sceite in aice le struchtúir tógtha imreoir, mar shampla táblaí crafting agus tinte campa.

english: Sitting is the safest way to travel while on a boat.
irish: Is é suí an bealach is sábháilte chun taisteal agus ar bhád.

english: Upon your arrival in Valheim, try to find stones and branches on the ground to build your first weapon.
irish: Ar do theacht i Valheim, déan iarracht clocha agus brainsí a aimsiú ar an talamh chun do chéad arm a thógáil.

english: It is generally a bad idea to venture outside at night...
irish: Tá sé i gcoitinne droch-smaoineamh chun fiontair taobh amuigh san oíche...

english: Hunting deer with a ranged weapon provides a good source of meat and skin.
irish: Soláthraíonn fianna le arm raonta foinse mhaith feola agus craicinn.

english: Build a rudimentary shelter as soon as possible!
irish: Tógáil foscadh rudimentary chomh luath agus is féidir!

english: Different enemies are weak to different damage types. For instance, Greydwarfs don't like fire.
irish: Tá naimhde éagsúla lag do chineálacha damáiste éagsúla. Mar shampla, nach bhfuil Greydwarfs cosúil le tine.

english: When you have built a bed, do not forget to claim it.
irish: Nuair a thóg tú leaba, ná déan dearmad é a éileamh.

english: Attacking with knives and bows while sneaking confers a large damage bonus.
irish: Ag ionsaí le sceana agus bows agus tugann sneaking bónas damáiste mór.
